In this file, we will quickly view the locations
```{python}
# Package Import
import folium
import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
import os
import numpy as np

# Data Import
city_info = pd.read_csv("../data/city_info.csv")
```

Build a quick map to view the locations:

```{python}
# Define bounding box limits
lon_min, lon_max = -95, -75
lat_min, lat_max = 30, 44

# Filter data to only include stations within the bounding box
city_info_filtered = city_info[
    (city_info['Lon'] >= lon_min) & (city_info['Lon'] <= lon_max) &
    (city_info['Lat'] >= lat_min) & (city_info['Lat'] <= lat_max)
]

# Define special cities to highlight
highlight_cities = ["Asheville", "Chattanooga", "Bluefield", "Beckley"]

# Create base map centered on filtered locations
center_lat = (lat_min + lat_max) / 2
center_lon = (lon_min + lon_max) / 2
m = folium.Map(location=[center_lat, center_lon], zoom_start=5)

# Add filtered city markers
for _, row in city_info_filtered.iterrows():
    if row['Name'] in highlight_cities:
        # Highlighted cities — larger and red
        folium.CircleMarker(
            location=[row['Lat'], row['Lon']],
            radius=9,               # larger size
            color='darkred',        # outline color
            fill=True,
            fill_color='red',
            fill_opacity=0.9,
            weight=2,
            popup=row['Name']
        ).add_to(m)
    else:
        # Regular cities — smaller and blue
        folium.CircleMarker(
            location=[row['Lat'], row['Lon']],
            radius=5,
            color='blue',
            fill=True,
            fill_color='blue',
            fill_opacity=1,
            weight=1,
            popup=row['Name']
        ).add_to(m)

# Add red rectangle bounding box
bounds = [[lat_min, lon_min], [lat_max, lon_max]]
folium.Rectangle(
    bounds=bounds,
    color='red',
    weight=2,
    fill=False
).add_to(m)

# Display the map
m

# Save map to use in the presentation
#m.save("../figures/city_map_full_us.html")
```

Let's take historical weather data from each of these selected weather stations, and make time series plots of precipitation:

``` {python}
# Define weather-retrieving and time series plotting function:

def station_time_series_plot(station_name):

    '''
    ARGUMENT:
    station_name -- string -- the name (town name ONLY, no ", XX" state name attachment) of a weather station in ROI
        * Note: Capitalize the first letter, e.g. "Asheville"
    '''
  
    # Retrieve weather station data
    ## build file path
    base_dir = os.path.join("..", "data", "ghcn_roi_daily_data")
    file_path = os.path.join(base_dir, f"{station_name}.csv")
    
    if not os.path.exists(file_path):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"No CSV file found for station '{station_name}' at {file_path}")
    
    ## read CSV file into dataframe
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
    def parse_custom_year(date_str):
        try:
            parts = date_str.split("/")
            mm, dd, yy = int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]), int(parts[2])
            
            # Apply custom rule for years
            if 59 <= yy <= 99:
                year = 1900 + yy
            else:  # 00–25
                year = 2000 + yy
            
            return pd.Timestamp(year=year, month=mm, day=dd)
        except Exception:
            return pd.NaT

    # Apply to the column
    df["date"] = df["date"].apply(parse_custom_year)
    ## Flag difference in days (to later avoid plotting inconsistencies for gaps)
    df["date_diff"] = df["date"].diff().dt.days

    # Add data required for 3-day rolling precip curve
    rolling_window = 3
    rolling_sum = df["precipitation"].rolling(window=rolling_window, min_periods=1).sum()


    ## ID gaps in time series to prevent plotting later:
    valid = [True] * len(df)

    for i in range(len(df)):
        # Look at the last `rolling_window-1` diffs
        if i >= 1:
            diffs = df["date_diff"].iloc[max(1, i-rolling_window+1):i+1]
            if (diffs > 1).any():  # gap detected
                valid[i] = False

    df["precip_3day_sum"] = rolling_sum
    df.loc[~np.array(valid), "precip_3day_sum"] = np.nan

    # Conversion constant
    MM_TO_INCH = 1 / 25.4

    # Create subplot layout with secondary y-axes enabled
    fig = make_subplots(
        rows=2, cols=1,
        shared_xaxes=True,
        vertical_spacing=0.08,
        subplot_titles=(
            "Daily Precipitation",
            "3-Day Rolling Sum of Precipitation"
        ),
        specs=[[{"secondary_y": True}], [{"secondary_y": True}]]
    )

    # --- Top plot: daily values ---
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=df["date"],
            y=df["precipitation"],
            mode="lines",
            name="Daily Precipitation (mm)",
            line=dict(color="#1f77b4")
        ),
        row=1, col=1, secondary_y=False
    )

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=df["date"],
            y=df["precipitation"] * MM_TO_INCH,
            mode="lines",
            name="Daily Precipitation (in)",
            line=dict(color="#1f77b4", dash="dot"),
            opacity=0.6
        ),
        row=1, col=1, secondary_y=True
    )

    fig.update_yaxes(showgrid=False, row=1, col=1, secondary_y=True)

    # --- Bottom plot: 3-day rolling sum ---
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=df["date"],
            y=df["precip_3day_sum"],
            mode="lines",
            name="3-Day Rolling Sum (mm)",
            line=dict(color="#ff7f0e")
        ),
        row=2, col=1, secondary_y=False
    )

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            x=df["date"],
            y=df["precip_3day_sum"] * MM_TO_INCH,
            mode="lines",
            name="3-Day Rolling Sum (in)",
            line=dict(color="#ff7f0e", dash="dot"),
            opacity=0.6
        ),
        row=2, col=1, secondary_y=True
    )

    # Layout and styling
    fig.update_layout(
        title=dict(
            text=f"Historical Precipitation Time Series - {station_name}",
            x=0.5,
        ),
        template="plotly_white",
        hovermode="x unified",
        font=dict(
        family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif",  # primary font + fallbacks
        size=14,        # global font size
        color="black"   # font color
        ),
        height=750,
        legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=-0.2, xanchor="center", x=0.5),
        margin=dict(t=120, l=60, r=60, b=60)
    )
    fig.update_yaxes(showgrid=False, row=2, col=1, secondary_y=True)

    # Axis labels
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Precipitation (mm)", row=1, col=1, secondary_y=False)
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Precipitation (in)", row=1, col=1, secondary_y=True)
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="3-Day Sum (mm)", row=2, col=1, secondary_y=False)
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="3-Day Sum (in)", row=2, col=1, secondary_y=True)
    fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Date", row=2, col=1)

    return fig
```

asheville_time_series_precip_plot = station_time_series_plot("Asheville")
asheville_time_series_precip_plot
